item.title: Madang Governor calls for devolution of powers from Waigani to provinces
item.description: Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa has called for the devolution of certain powers from Waigani to the provinces to enable provincial governments to manage their own affairs. He said this yesterday whilst launching a 20- footer container full of medical drugs at the Madang Provincial Hospital.
item.content:encoded:
Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa has called for the devolution of certain powers from Waigani to the provinces to enable provincial governments to manage their own affairs.

He said this yesterday whilst launching a 20- footer container full of medical drugs at the Madang Provincial Hospital.

Governor Pariwa appealed to the national government to devolve and decentralise certain powers to the provincial governments so they can look after their own people.

"I know the National Medicine Policy states that the procurement powers for medical supplies is the responsibility of the National Department of Health, but we can not continue to sit and wait on Waigani to help us.

"You cannot manage the country from Waigani. You cannot run Papua New Guinea from Waigani. It is hard, and that is why we are gathered here. Serious decentralisation approach must take place so that we can be given enough powers to attend to our people's needs," Governor Pariwa said.

He said the Madang government has responded to the situation at the provincial hospital when it scaled down services and presented container of medicines to the board and management of the Madang Provincial Health Authority.

The purchase of the medical supplies was made possible with funding assistance from the Governor's Provincial Support Improvement Program (PSIP) funds.

Pariwa said another container will be delivered in the coming one or two months and assured the people that the govermnment will continue to support the health sector in the province to make sure people get the services they deserve.

The Madang Government has also assisted in rebuilding the children's ward and in purchasing two Southern Cross tanks, which have helped alleviate the hospital's water woes.

Present to witness the launch was Deputy Board Chairman of MaPHA, Young Wadau, Director of Curative Health Services, Dr Jiuth Gawi, Acting Executive Director of the Madang Provincial Hospital, Jeremiah Johnmark, senior medical officers and hospital staff.

Speaking on behalf of MaPHA's CEO, Dr Martin Daimen, who is out of the province, Dr Gawi applauded Governor Pariwa and his government for always stepping in to assist whenever the hospital is in dire need of help.

Deputy Board Chairman, Young Wadau highlighted the need for MaPHA to start exploring possible means of revenue- generation to help sustain its operations when government funds are slow in coming in.

He added, "We all face this problem of no money, no medicine, etc. We have not looked deeper down into ourselves, from the executive management, the board to see how we can make money.

"Madang PHA is a corporate entity made by the Act of Parliament and it can formulate business to make money on its own. We have not gone to that path that's why we are saying no money, no money.

"We are looking at the national government, we are asking the business entities to help us, and they do come out but very reluctantly. When the money comes in, it is all misappropriated. And I am not going to take apology for saying that." Chairman Wadau said.

item.title: El Nino peak moved
item.description: The prolonged dry season is said to become strongest in November and December, instead of August and September as previously forecasted. Papua New Guinea declared El Nino on June 16 this year, with the forecast indicating it will be strong between August and September.
item.content:encoded:
The prolonged dry season is said to become strongest in November and December, instead of August and September as previously forecasted.

Papua New Guinea declared El Nino on June 16 this year, with the forecast indicating it will be strong between August and September.

National Weather Service Director, Jimmy Gomoga says El Nino is yet to reach its peak when giving an update on the current weather pattern on NBC Talk Back today.

“We declared the El Nino on the 16th of June this year, and since then it has been developing.

“We have not reached the peak, it's still going towards its peak, and the El Nino should peak around November, December. It has shifted a bit, we were saying August, September, but it's now November and December.” Gomoga said.

Gomoga explained why this is happening and moved as to was earlier predicted.

“We normally monitor the area called 3.4, it's in the central and pacific region around Tahiti.

“We also monitor that region to ensure that the surface temperatures, when they reach about 0.8 degrees, then we know that it has gone into El Nino conditions, it has already reached El Nino thresholds.” Gomoga said.

He said the dry season is expected to end in April or May of 2027.

“From the data, especially around 3.4, the area that we are monitoring, the ocean temperatures for El Nino, the data shows that it's going to reach the peak in November, December.

“It will begin to decay around January, February, and then by April, May, we should be able to exit. But it might, but the impacts, not that it might, but when it ends in April, May, then the impact will still remain throughout the dry season.” He said.

The weather service is closely monitoring El Nino as it continues to develop.

item.title: PNG broadcaster joins Asia-Pacific media visit in China
item.description: Foreign journalists from across the Asia-Pacific and Euro-Asia regions are in Chengdu, Sichuan province, China, to explore the country’s advances in science, technology and innovation, and its cooperation with Belt and Road partner countries. The Asia-Pacific delegation including 24 journalists from 21 countries, including Papua New Guinea’s National Broadcasting Corporation.
item.content:encoded:
Foreign journalists from across the Asia-Pacific and Euro-Asia regions are in Chengdu, Sichuan province, China, to explore the country’s advances in science, technology and innovation, and its cooperation with Belt and Road partner countries.

The Asia-Pacific delegation including 24 journalists from 21 countries, including Papua New Guinea’s National Broadcasting Corporation.

Euro-Asia regions are in Chengdu for a four-day media visit focusing on science, technology, innovation and international cooperation.

The program is taking journalists to research institutions, technology companies and innovation facilities under the Chengdu–Chongqing Belt and Road Science, Technology and Innovation Cooperation Zone.

The visit includes clean-energy research, agricultural biotechnology, biomedical industries, robotics and artificial intelligence, as well as China’s giant panda conservation program.

They will also visit a technology-transfer centre to learn how Chinese science and innovation are being shared with international partners.

The final day will focus on space technology, satellites and solar energy, including smart manufacturing.

The visit is providing international media with an opportunity to observe China’s scientific and technological development and consider its relevance to development in their own countries.

item.title: Ohana Foundation takes El Nino preparedness awareness to village level
item.description: An El Nino preparedness and mitigation awareness was taken to Malmal Village, outside Madang town, to encourage community members to prepare for the challenges associated with prolonged dry conditions. item.content:encoded:
An El Nino preparedness and mitigation awareness was taken to Malmal Village, outside Madang town, to encourage community members to prepare for the challenges associated with prolonged dry conditions.

Members of the Ohana Foundation, together with Mr and Miss DWU 2026 contestants, have led the initiative focused on helping the community understand what El Nino is, the science behind the weather phenomenon, and how it can affect water supply, food gardens, health, and everyday life.

During the awareness, the team also highlighted the importance of communities looking out for one another and taking practical steps to protect their families during the difficult season.

Malmal community leader Frankie Duadak told the awareness team that the community relies heavily on water wells as its main source of water.

He said the community has separate wells, with one used for drinking and another for washing clothes and other household activities.

Mr Duadak also explained that the current dry conditions have severely affected food gardens in the community.

He recalled the severe drought of 1997, saying the situation reminded him of the challenges communities faced at that time when food gardens and banana plants were badly affected.

Ms DWU 2026 Marcia Normal, explained to the community the importance of understanding El Nino and taking precautions to protect themselves.

“When we don't have enough water, we will hardly find water for drinking, cooking, and washing. We all rely on garden food, so when there is no rain, garden food will be affected,” she told the community.

Mr DWU 2026 Gini Sega, encouraged the people of Malmal to prepare ahead by finding suitable containers and drums to collect and safely store rainwater whenever rain comes.

He said proper water storage would help families have access to clean water for essential activities such as drinking and cooking during periods when water becomes scarce.

The founder and director of the Ohana Foundation and Female Vice President of the DWU Student Representative Council, Theresha Orere said the awareness was a student-led initiative aimed at empowering communities with knowledge during a difficult period.

She said that whilst community members received the information openly, one of the major concerns raised was the lack of institutional support reaching communities facing the impacts of El Nino.

She said awareness could encourage people to look after their water and prepare themselves, but there was also a bigger question about whether responsible authorities could provide practical relief and support to affected communities.

The foundation said students would like to do more to assist communities such as Malmal, but their capacity is limited, with knowledge and awareness being the main resources they can currently provide.

The awareness highlighted the importance of combining community preparedness and education with stronger institutional support to help vulnerable communities navigate the impacts of El Nino.

item.title: Waritzian School to expand into junior high
item.description: Waritzian Primary School in Markham district, Morobe province, is preparing to expand into junior high school education, giving children from the community and nearby villages a chance to continue their education closer to home. The school is nearing completion of a new four-in-one classroom building, which is expected to accommodate Grade 9 students from 2027, subject to approval from education a
item.content:encoded:
Waritzian Primary School in Markham district, Morobe province, is preparing to expand into junior high school education, giving children from the community and nearby villages a chance to continue their education closer to home.

The school is nearing completion of a new four-in-one classroom building, which is expected to accommodate Grade 9 students from 2027, subject to approval from education authorities.

For families in Waritzian and surrounding communities, the expansion could reduce the need for children to travel to other areas to continue their secondary education after completing primary school.

The Markham District Development Authority has provided K200,000 towards the classroom project.

Local carpenters and workers are carrying out the construction, allowing people from the community to use their skills while helping build facilities for the next generation of students.

If construction is completed and the required approvals are secured, Waritzian Primary School will begin its first Grade 9 intake in 2027.

The expansion is expected to provide more children in the area with access to secondary education closer to their homes, reducing the distance some families currently face when sending their children to school.

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape has appealed to landowners of the Papua LNG gas development to resolve any issues among themselves before the launch of the Final Investment Decision [FID] in November of this year.

Speaking at Government House last Thursday, the Prime Minister appealed to landowners of the Papua LNG gas development, from Central and Gulf provinces, to work with leaders in their respective provinces as well as the minister for Petroleum, Jimmy Maladina, to resolve any disagreements that they may have.

“The Government must secure agreements to allow project operators to announce the Final Investment Decision [FID] and raise funding to deliver Papua LNG,” he said.

Marape said the construction of the project will commence following the successful delivery of the FID from the project operators.

According to Prime Minister, the Government also successfully negotiated with the Japanese Crude Cocktail to reduce the 9% price of gas sale to 5%.

item.title: Hakena and Hyun claim U16 Singles title
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s junior tennis players Colita Hakena and Thomas Hyun have secured the U16 Girls’ and Boys’ singles titles following the conclusion of the 2026 KPHL PNG Junior Tennis Championships in Port Moresby. The Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited-sponsored event saw Hakena defeat another rising talent and national teammate, Rehoni Josepha Rumbam, who finished as runner-up, while Adelaide Mesa
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s junior tennis players Colita Hakena and Thomas Hyun have secured the U16 Girls’ and Boys’ singles titles following the conclusion of the 2026 KPHL PNG Junior Tennis Championships in Port Moresby.

The Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited-sponsored event saw Hakena defeat another rising talent and national teammate, Rehoni Josepha Rumbam, who finished as runner-up, while Adelaide Mesa finished third.

Hyun maintained the lead to secure the title ahead of Arthur Wash and Ivan Mera, who finished as runners-up in the U16 Boys’ singles.

Hyun also finished as runner-up with teammate Irene Jose in the Mixed Doubles, followed by Hakena and her teammate Jemimah Bakani. The winners of this category were Wash and Mera.

The PNG Tennis Association-sanctioned event saw young talents from Port Moresby, Lae and Goroka compete at the Port Moresby Racquets Club during the three-day tournament, showing determination and great sportsmanship on court.

In a social media post, the PNG Tennis Association thanked all players, parents, coaches, officials, volunteers and supporters who helped make this year’s championships a success.

“We are proud to see the talent, friendships and sportsmanship developing through junior tennis, and we look forward to seeing all back on court at the next tournament,” the Tennis Association said.

Meanwhile, in the other singles divisions, the Junior Under-10 Boys’ event saw Lawrence Rumbam finish on top, while Edison Teh and Bjarne Refshauge finished second and third respectively.

The U10 Girls’ title was won by Maria Belen, with another Hakena, Hebrew-Bulang, finishing as runner-up. Kiara Tikari finished third.

In the U12 Singles, Jayce Josiah Yuill, Firenze Hanafi and Aaditya Agrawal took the medals, while the girls’ event saw Mika Tabuchi finish on top, ahead of Gima Kilaverave and Beulah Ireng in the U12 Girls’ division.

River-Jordan Hakena claimed top spot in the U14 Boys’ singles against national teammates Timothy Koliwan and Andrew Aisi, while Macklyn Meninga did the same for the U14 Girls’, securing first place over Melisa Nimi and Susan Geita.

In the other Mixed Doubles results, Aaditya Agrawal and Firenze Hanafi claimed the U12 Mixed Doubles title over Beulah Ireng and Mika Tabuchi, while Elijah Mera and Jayce Josiah Yuill finished in third place.

Aisi and Koliwan teamed up in the U14 Mixed Doubles, taking out the title against Ipai Matte and Macklyn Meninga, while River-Jordan Hakena and Matrus Pataba finished as runners-up.

item.title: Pala takes ICC lessons into Garamuts campaign

Pala travelled to Malaysia on August 16 for the intensive one-week programme, joining coaches from different cricketing nations, including former national coaches, two former Pakistan
item.content:encoded:
Cricket PNG Garamuts Head Coach Kila Pala has reflected on his recent ICC Level 3 Coaching Course in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, after returning home and leading the U19 Garamuts to qualification for ICC EAP Division 1.

Pala travelled to Malaysia on August 16 for the intensive one-week programme, joining coaches from different cricketing nations, including former national coaches, two former Pakistan international players and a current Afghanistan Test player.

Following completion of the in-course component, Pala returned to PNG and joined the U19 Garamuts. The team travelled to Vanuatu to compete in the ICC EAP Division 2 Qualifier.

The Garamuts secured qualification for Division 1 on September 12.

The international coaching experience, followed by the Garamuts’ successful EAP campaign, adds to PNG’s continued investment in developing coaching capacity and strengthening the pathway for the country’s next generation of cricketers.

Reflecting on the course, Pala said his biggest takeaways were keeping players at the centre, the role of coaches in creating problems for players to solve, self-reflection and understanding everything involved in a High-Performance setup.

“The biggest takeout from the course for me was the players at the centre of focus.”

Pala said the experience was highly informative and he hopes to pass the knowledge gained on to PNG players and coaches.

His ICC Level 3 qualification is now entering its final stage, with a 12-week post-course project. Participants have been placed into groups and allocated a Master Tutor to guide them through the project.

Pala acknowledged Cricket PNG Board and Management, sponsors, High Performance staff and the media for their continued support.
